card.title: TOTTORI REGIMENT
card.flavorText: The 53rd Infantry Regiment (Tottori) was part of the 17th Division of the Imperial Japanese Army during WWII. During the Pacific War, the 17th Division consisted of the 53rd, 54th, and 81st Infantry Regiments, supported by various other units including artillery, engineers, transport, and tanks. In September 1943, the division was assigned to the Southern Expeditionary Army Group and sent to New Britain in the Islands Region of Papua New Guinea, operating under the command of the 8th Area Army based in Rabaul. The first two convoys arrived in New Britain safely in 1943. However, the third convoy was ambushed by the USS Grayback submarine, resulting in the sinking of the auxiliary cruiser Awata Maru and the loss of 1,087 men from the 17th Division. The remaining units, led by Lieutenant General Iwao Matsuda, participated in the Battle of Cape Gloucester and the Battle of New Britain, eventually being reduced to a few independent mixed regiments guarding hospital areas. The survivors of the 17th Division surrendered to Allied forces in New Britain by the end of the war on August 15, 1945.
